STEP 1 - Scene: A small plated snack/side of raw-looking broccoli florets and a whole pear-shaped green fruit (looks like a pear or green apple-type fruit). Not a full cooked meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across at its width. Area ≈ 26 x 26 ≈ 530 cm² (treating it as a dinner plate; the plate is square-ish, so this is approximate).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Broccoli florets (raw, a cluster of about 4–5 florets plus a small piece)
- Whole pear (green-yellow, medium size, roughly 7–8 cm tall and 7 cm wide)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Broccoli: florets cover roughly 90 cm²... (about 17% of vessel area)
- Pear: roughly 50 cm² visible footprint (about 9%)
- Total food coverage ≈ 26%, which is consistent with a small amount on a large plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Broccoli: 90 cm² x 4 cm ≈ 360 ml gross envelope (florets are airy)
- Pear: whole fruit volume roughly 7 x 7 x 7.5 cm ≈ 250 ml (ellipsoid ~0.52 x 7 x 7 x 7.5 ≈ 191 ml; use ~200 ml)

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Broccoli: 360 ml x 0.5 ≈ 180 g. Recheck against a single medium-size broccoli head of this kind; the visible florets are closer to 90–110 g, so use ~100 g.
- Pear: whole fruit ≈ 1 pear, about 170 g (density ~0.85 g/ml for whole fruit).

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Broccoli, raw: 34 kcal/100 g → 100 g = 34 kcal
- Pear, raw: 57 kcal/100 g → 170 g = 97 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 270 g total with roughly 130 kcal is plausible for one pear plus a small handful of broccoli on a plate. It is a small amount for a full plate, so the estimate is reasonable.

Total: ~270 g, ~131 kcal.
